html:
The Alawa are an Aboriginal people of southern Arnhem Land in the Northern Territory, in country along the lower Roper River and the Limmen Bight near the Gulf of Carpentaria.

Their neighbours included the Mangarrayi and Yangman upriver, and the Ngalakan and Ngandi to the north. Many Alawa people came to live at the Roper River mission, founded in 1908, which grew into the town of Ngukurr.

The suburb of Alawa in Darwin is named after them. For the long history before contact, see Aboriginal Australian societies.
sum: The Alawa are an Aboriginal people of southern Arnhem Land in the Northern Territory, in country along the lower Roper River and the Limmen Bight near the Gulf of Carpentaria.
